PROPOSED SKIP: gh.optimaero/optimaeropx4sil is a MATLAB/Simulink software-in-the-loop (SIL) example environment, not a device or a programmatically steppable environment that OpenMHS can drive. README.md:18: 'This repository houses a software in the loop (SIL) simulation for an aircraft using the PX4 controller and a Simulink-based physics plant, sensor, and environmental model. The purpose of this SIL is to provide the user with an example of how to connect the PX4 flight controller to a Simulink plant model.' The simulation models are the binary Simulink files VehicleSilSimulation.slx and VehiclePlant.slx (README.md:18). The pinned tree at 1bcb568248390dac58e343d63b383c86a1821c23 has 176 files: 60 .slx, 47 .m, one .h, one .cpp, and no .py, .launch, .msg, .srv, .action or package.xml (git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD; the filtered listing is empty). There is no entry symbol, Python class or function, or environment registration to name as native: the card's entry_symbols and models are empty, and MHS/registry/repos/robots/optimaero__optimaeropx4sil.json records NO_ENTRY_SYMBOL and NO_INSTALL_FILE.

The only device-facing runtime path is the PX4 SIL connector, a MATLAB MEX S-function built with 'mex -I./includes pixhawk_sil_connector.cpp' (PX4SILConnector/make.m:4). It uses MAVLink (PX4SILConnector/SILConnector.h:12) over a TCP acceptor on port 4560 (SILConnector.h:97), with QGroundControl on UDP 18570 (PX4SILConnector/README.md:40). This is MAVLink, not ROS. The parent tree declares no ROS endpoint, type, launch file or node: 'git grep -i -E rclcpp|rospy|std_msgs|sensor_msgs|rosbridge|ros::|ros2|catkin|colcon HEAD -- . :!PX4-Autopilot' exits 1 with no match, and the pinned tree contains no .launch, .msg, .srv, .action or package.xml file. The registry card lists ROS 2, but that material is not in the card's pinned tree: .gitmodules:1-3 declares PX4-Autopilot as a submodule, and the pinned tree records it only as the gitlink '160000 commit fd9e16a0a2fd29af33586524ed7ab662985365e1 PX4-Autopilot'. The gate's UpstreamTree at 1bcb... reports kind=git, pinned=True, 176 files, zero files under PX4-Autopilot/, and read_text('PX4-Autopilot/package.xml') returns None. A source_ref into that submodule would be G4.REF_MISSING; even if it were readable, it would describe PX4 Autopilot ROS 2 topics, not this SIL's interface. The second .gitmodules entry (px4-autopilot, lines 4-6) has no gitlink in the pinned tree.

The SIL cannot run on the card's target platform or without proprietary MATLAB: README.md:20 says the Windows installation 'will fail on Mac, as Matlab does not support Mac for all required toolboxes'; README.md:115-123 requires the Aerospace Toolbox, Aerospace Blockset, Simulink, Simulink Test, UAV Toolbox, Instrument Control Toolbox and the MATLAB MinGW-w64 compiler; initVehicleSIL.m:69-74 lists the same tools, :78-93 refuses to run when they are absent, and :96-100 requires a C++ mex compiler. The card's install has no commands and platform linux, while the model is opened and run in MATLAB (README.md:101-103) alongside PX4 in WSL 2 (PX4SILConnector/README.md:7-14 and :37-45). The upstream-sim strategy is a MATLAB GUI workflow, not a Python factory the SDK can open.

This is the same class of repository as the registry's skipped MATLAB/Simulink cards: gh.mathworks-robotics/mujoco-simulink-blockset (MHS/registry/overrides/robots.json:3928: 'not a Python device driver, and it ships no Python wrapper') and gh.simenandresen/simulink-underwater-robotics-simulator (robots.json:5851: 'MATLAB/Simulink-only ... with no Python wrapper or hardware transport'). A RosDriver would have to invent ROS endpoints and a device that the pinned tree does not contain; a direct Driver has no Python class or function to wrap; a GymnasiumDriver would have to invent a task, action space, reward and terminal semantics because the repository registers no environment and steps the simulation inside Simulink, not Python. The rules forbid inventing those interfaces and bounds.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card says family-config with family=ros and helper=RosDriver, but the pinned parent tree has no ROS endpoint/type/launch declaration and no Python class or function to wrap; this is therefore a proposed skip rather than a RosDriver package. No package code was written and no gate was run: the required driver.py/fake.py/facts.md/test_driver.py cannot be honestly created from this tree. task.json is unchanged. The clone at 1bcb568248390dac58e343d63b383c86a1821c23 was left unmodified ('git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no' is empty; nothing was written under the clone or its .git), and no upstream code was imported, installed or run. No network, pip install or hardware was used. This is a model-authored skip proposal for registry override review (model deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run ros-wave-c-079); no human review, hardware run or publication approval is claimed.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Accepted the skip proposal (NOT_A_DEVICE). The repository's own content is a MATLAB/Simulink software-in-the-loop example that connects a modified PX4 to Simulink plant models (README.md:18): outside the submodule the working copy holds 60 .slx and 47 .m files, XML, images, PDFs and a pixhawk_sil_connector C++ MEX source with a prebuilt .mexw64, and no Python, launch, message, service or package.xml file, no entry symbol and no callable API; the simulation runs inside MATLAB. The working copy also contains the checked-out PX4-Autopilot submodule (.gitmodules), the modified PX4 v1.14.0 fork the README names, which the author's count of the parent tree did not mention; that flight stack is driven through the gh.px4/px4-autopilot card's MAVLink route, not through this repository. The reviewer proposes the matching skip override and changed no authored file; the reviewer's gate run created check-report.json (G1, G2, G3 and G9 fail because there is no package; stable digest sha256:7f1320bf338e51d6c0284ded1e5dbba81242fb0c318825f46e7c02d1dc343517). For the human reviewer: No package code exists. The plant models (an F-16 and a hexarotor) run only inside MATLAB with Simulink toolboxes; the PX4 SIL connector is a Windows MEX binary built from pixhawk_sil_connector.cpp.
